title: Head of Engineering, Rewards
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why South Africa South Africa has one of the strongest engineering communities anywhere in the world, and we are deliberately growing our technology organisation in the country. We already have several team members based here. The work is fully remote, and the mission we are working on is a good deal closer to home than it is for our teams elsewhere. So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Rewards to join us in South Africa. About The Role Rewards is one of the most strategically important platforms at Moniepoint, and it is being built into a dedicated charter with its own engineering and product leadership. The platform sits at the centre of our retention strategy across a user base of approximately 23 million people. Today the platform does one thing: cashback. It works, but it has barely scratched the surface of what rewards can be, and the cashback product itself is not yet built to the depth it deserves. The ambition is to evolve it into a full rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform — and to do that across the full 360 degrees of our network. That means rewards for our business customers, rewards for our consumer customers, and rewards for the sales agents who drive our distribution. Very few companies get to design this from close to a blank page at this scale. The Head of Engineering owns that platform end to end. You will inherit a team of nine engineers, including an Engineering Manager, and build the organisation out from there — the current expectation is a minimum of three product units and upwards of 25 people, though the eventual shape is genuinely yours to define. Your first objective is to get the best possible performance out of the cashback product we already have. From there, you will work with Growth, Sales and Marketing to determine what we build for acquisition and retention, and roll it out across every customer we serve. This is a consumer-facing product engineering role, and that is the most important thing to understand about it. Rewards is won or lost on experimentation, personalisation, and the quality of the experience in a customer's hands. We are looking for a leader who has built and shipped direct-to-consumer products at scale, who is fluent in experimentation and A/B testing, and who has real depth in front-end and mobile engineering — not a purely backend platform leader. Moniepoint runs a Domain CTO model. We view our Heads of Engineering as the CTO of their domain: you own the technical roadmap, the architecture, the delivery, and the organisation beneath you. You will have full autonomy over engineering strategy, architecture, hiring, operating cadence and roadmap trade-offs. You will report functionally to our Group CTO, with a dual reporting line into the Product leader for Rewards. That second line is a delivery relationship rather than a seniority one — engineering and product are peers here, and you will build the team to full capacity together. Your responsibilities as Head of Engineering, Rewards includes: Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Rewards Platform end to end. Improving the performance, reliability and depth of the existing cashback product as an immediate first priority. Evolving cashback into a broader rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform serving business customers, consumer customers and sales agents. Building the engineering organisation from its current base - structuring product units, hiring engineers and Engineering Managers, and leading through those managers as the team scales. Establishing a strong experimentation culture: A/B testing, cohort analysis, and measurement that lets the team learn quickly what actually changes customer behaviour. Working closely with Growth, Sales and Marketing to translate acquisition and retention objectives into product and engineering initiatives. Owning the customer-facing experience of rewards across mobile and web, including how quickly and reliably customers receive what they have earned. Define architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and own the engineering health of the domain — incidents, production defects, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and developer experience. Build the platform to serve customers across multiple geographies as Moniepoint expands. Partner with Product to define the rewards-specific metrics and OKRs that do not yet exist, and hold the team to them. Who You Are  Direct-to-consumer product engineering at scale. You have built and shipped products used directly by large consumer audiences, and you understand what moves engagement and retention. This is the defining requirement of the role. Genuine front-end and mobile depth. You have led or personally built consumer-facing mobile and web experiences. A backend-only background, however strong, is not what this role needs. Experimentation and growth engineering. Hands-on experience running A/B tests, feature flagging, and measurement frameworks, and using the results to drive product decisions rather than to justify them. At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, not a single team. Hands-on technical leadership. You are still close to the code. We expect a meaningful proportion of hands-on engineering time and technical credibility with the engineers you lead. 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams through growth phases. Comfort with our backend environment — Java and Spring Boot — and the ability to lead backend engineers credibly, even if it is not where your own depth sits. Experience building and scaling an engineering organisation from a small base, including hiring and developing Engineering Managers. Strong collaboration with commercial stakeholders — growth, marketing and sales — and the ability to translate business objectives into engineering work. Rewards, loyalty, gamification, personalisation or growth platform experience is a strong advantage but is not required. Fintech or payments experience is an advantage, not a requirement. Cultural Alignment As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality. Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early. Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders. No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes. Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. What Success Looks Like In The Role The existing cashback product performing measurably better — faster, more reliable, and more compelling to customers. A credible rewards platform roadmap defined with Product, and the first initiatives beyond cashback shipped. A functioning experimentation practice, where the team ships, measures and learns on a short cycle. An engineering organisation built out from its current base, with a strong bench of Engineering Managers and senior engineers. Rewards established as a measurable contributor to retention and engagement across the customer base. Clear architecture standards and engineering processes in place across the product units. Why Join Us A rare blank page. The platform exists, but almost everything it could become is still ahead of it, and you will define what that is. Direct influence on retention across a base of roughly 23 million users, at one of the largest and fastest-growing digital banks in Africa. title: Head of Personal Banking Sales Network
description: Who we are Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira’s in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. Moniepoint is Africa's all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. In 2023, we processed $182 billion and are Nigeria's largest merchant acquirer. About the Role The Head of Personal Banking Sales Network is an experienced sales professional who owns the retail sales distribution engine for personal banking. This is a network leadership role, not an individual selling role and you will be required to build, motivate and control a large independent contractor field force and the regional management layer above it. You will be measured on qualified customer acquisition and product penetration delivered at a defensible cost per unit.  Duties & Responsibilities Own end-to-end performance of the sales team: deliver the acquisition and transaction target through the field sales channel. Own agent productivity: acquisitions per active agent per month, share of field agents performing 100% vs target, and time to first sale for new agents. Own network health: active agent count, attrition, reactivation and coverage in priority cities Design and maintain territory structure, prioritising penetration in priority cities. Set recruitment targets for each city/cluster and ensure delivery versus the target. Own cost per acquisition through the sales channel, including commission, incentive and field support. Design commission and incentive structures that reward activated and transacting customers, not registrations. Ensure full compliance with all legal and regulatory requirements. Own the field sales performance routines: daily check-ins, weekly regional reviews, monthly business reviews. Requirements 10 - 15 years in field sales leadership, with at least 5 years leading regional sales leaders. Direct experience running a distributed agent, agency or independent contractor network of significant scale. Proven ownership of a commission or incentive scheme, including designing it and defending its cost. Strong command of sales analytics: funnel conversion, productivity distribution, cohort based performance. Strong people leadership skills: training, motivating and managing a large field sales team Experience operating in financial services, telecoms, FMCG distribution or another high volume regulated or semi regulated industry. Willingness to travel across regions regularly. Preferred Qualifications Experience in banking, payments or lending distribution in Nigeria. Experience in building and scaling a field sales team Familiarity with sales enablement tooling and CRM based territory management. About You You’re calm, objective, and grounded, even in high stakes situations. You balance empathy with fairness and have strong judgment on what’s “right” versus what’s “easy.” You communicate with clarity and confidence, building trust at every level. You think systemically and you see patterns behind cases and design solutions that prevent recurrence. You value compliance but see your role as enabling business success, not blocking it. What Success Looks Like Delivery against monthly and annual first transaction targets from the sales channel. An implemented plan to increase agent output, featuring defined benchmarks and measurable tactical growth drivers. Established field sales performance routines, including weekly and monthly reviews, executed against standardized templates with disciplined action tracking. Optimized cost per new active customer, trending within the approved thresholds.

title: Head, POS Recovery
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: POS Recovery Manager Department: POS Channel Reports to: VP, POS Channel About this role: This role owns the end-to-end recovery of non-performing POS terminal assets — from the moment a terminal is flagged as at risk through to physical retrieval, financial settlement, and post-write-off recovery. Responsibilities Recovery Strategy Governance Own the terminal recovery lifecycle that defines escalation speed and settlement windows based on terminal age, transaction history, and recovery economics.  Ensure every terminal that enters recovery mode is assigned, tracked, escalated on schedule, and settled within its gate deadline — recovery, write-off, paid write-off, or insurance claim.  Design and continuously refine the recovery strategy, covering device collection, swap logistics, sales agent coordination, external agency management, and the efficient flow of assets back to custody.  Field Team Leadership Lead, manage, and hold accountable a distributed field recovery team across multiple regions.  Instill a culture of operational discipline, accountability, and ethical conduct. Recovery work involves sensitive situations (confronting custodians about lost assets, handling disputes, managing bounty payments); the team must operate with integrity.  Develop comprehensive standard operating procedures for every recovery scenario: BRM-led recovery, external agency coordination, business takeover, faulty terminal collection, voluntary write-off processing, dispute handling, revive processing.  Build training programmes for recovery agents covering: terminal identification, check-in procedures, evidence collection for disputes, GPS and field management tools, escalation protocols.  KPI Management and Recovery Economics Define and track recovery KPIs: recovery rate (pre-write-off), BRM recovery rate, external recovery rate, average days to recovery, cost per recovery, revive rate (post-write-off), bounty efficiency (bounty spend vs recovery value recovered).  Own the recovery economics: ensure total bounty spend plus logistics cost is always less than the recovery value of the terminals retrieved. The programme must be self-funding — recovery must generate more value than it costs.  Report monthly on: terminals entering recovery mode, terminals recovered, terminals written off, terminals revived, net financial impact, bounty spend, external agency spend, dispute volumes and outcomes.  Experience & Background Minimum 7 years of progressive experience managing large-scale field operations, logistics, asset recovery, or after-sales service, with at least 3 years in a senior leadership role.  Experience managing distributed field teams across multiple regions in Nigeria — you understand the infrastructure, the logistics constraints, and the human dynamics of field recovery operations.  Experience managing third-party service providers, contractors, or agency networks with performance-based contracts.  Direct experience in the Nigerian market with its specific logistical, regulatory, and operational realities.  Preferred: Experience from fintech, telecoms, e-commerce logistics, or any high-volume distributed asset management environment.  Preferred: Experience managing asset recovery at scale (thousands of units per month, not dozens).  Skills & Competencies Proven ability to design and implement structured operational processes (SOPs, escalation frameworks, settlement procedures) from scratch or through a major restructure.  Strong analytical capability — you use data to drive decisions, track performance, calculate ROI on recovery spend.  Financial discipline & budget management — experience managing a budget or cost centre, understanding unit economics, and demonstrating net positive recovery value.  Technical & Systems acumen — experience with product management/development lifecycles (writing briefs, working with engineers), GPS tracking, CRM, field management tools, or route optimisation platforms.  Regulatory & Compliance understanding — familiarity with insurance claim processes, write-off accounting, or asset disposal regulations in Nigeria.  What Success Looks Like in This Role Terminal recovery lifecycle is tightly governed, ensuring swift escalation and settlement within established gate deadlines.  Field recovery operations maintain high ethical standards and operational discipline across all regions.  Recovery program operates as a self-funding unit where total recovery value generated consistently exceeds total bounty and logistics expenditure.  Robust systems, SOPs, and field management tools are seamlessly integrated into daily team operations.  Transparent monthly reporting clearly demonstrates positive net financial impact and high recovery/revive rates.  Why Join Us?  Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.  Support for professional development and a dynamic culture driving financial inclusion across Africa.

title: Inventory Support Officer (Lagos)
description: Who We are Moniepoint Inc is a financial technology company digitizing Africa’s real economy by building a financial ecosystem for businesses, providing them with all the payment, banking, credit and business management tools they need to succeed.  What We do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community, dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We have several products that provide essential services for businesses such as credit, overdrafts etc. We leverage artificial intelligence and data to make our decisions but also have the technology and data-driven best practices used to support our businesses.  1A. Inventory Support Officer – POS Terminals Role Purpose The ISO (Terminals) is the dedicated custodian for all forms of POS terminals flowing through the repair pipeline. The role ensures end-to-end traceability, enforces custody controls, and maintains absolute logical–physical alignment within the Repair Centre's IMS subsystem, covering every stage from receipt of faulty units to dispatch of QA-cleared OK devices. Key Responsibilities Intake & Receipt Management Receive faulty/returned terminals from state offices; verify against the recall waybill at serial-number level before accepting into the IMS. Log all received devices in the IMS with correct status within 24 hours of physical arrival. Identify and quarantine damaged or missing-serial devices; raise a Discrepancy Report immediately. Repair Pipeline Tracking Push faulty devices to technicians daily and update IMS status to 'In Repair' upon assignment. Monitor movement of each terminal through all repair stages: Assessment → In Repair → Awaiting QA → QA Cleared → Dispatch Holding. Enforce the 24–72-hour SLA from receipt-to-assignment and from QA clearance-to-dispatch readiness. QA Integration & Status Management Receive QA-approved terminals and update IMS status to 'QA Cleared – Awaiting Dispatch' within 4 hours. Flag devices that fail QA back to the repair queue or classify as 'Beyond Economic Repair (BER)' with a written justification report. Ensure all 'BER' devices are tagged and isolated in the scrap/disposal holding area. Dispatch & Outbound Logistics Generate the Dispatch List and Waybill for QA-cleared refurbished and OK devices; obtain approval from Repair Centre Manager and Cluster lead before release. Scan all devices at serial level during physical loading; update IMS to 'In Transit – Outbound'. Confirm receipt acknowledgment from the destination state SIO and close the dispatch transaction in IMS. Inventory Counts & Reconciliation Conduct daily physical counts of all terminals in the repair centre; reconcile against IMS records. Escalate any variance (physical vs. logical) to the Lead, Inventory Support within the same business day. Participate in monthly, quarterly, and annual wall-to-wall counts as directed by the Inventory & Warehouse Manager. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain clearly labelled racks and segregated zones: Faulty, Under-Repair, Refurbished/OK, BER/Scrap. Enforce all provisions of the POS Inventory Control SOP within the repair centre. Uphold audit readiness, workplace safety, and environmental handling standards at all times. Reporting Line Functional: Lead, Inventory Support (Regional) Operational: Repair Centre Manager Dotted: Regional Inventory & Warehouse Manager   1B. Inventory Support Officer – Spare Parts Role Purpose The ISO (Spare Parts) manages the complete lifecycle of all repair consumables — batteries, screens, cables, and accessories — within the repair centre. The role ensures that technicians have the right parts at the right time, waste is minimised, and all issues are fully documented and traceable. Key Responsibilities Spare Parts Receipt & Storage Receive all incoming spare parts consignments; verify at batch/serial level against the accompanying delivery note before logging into IMS. Store spare parts in designated, labelled bins organised by part type and model compatibility. Ensure storage conditions protect electronic components from moisture, dust, and extreme temperature. Issuance Control Issue spare parts ONLY against an approved Job Card raised by a technician and validated by the Repair Centre Manager. Update IMS stock levels immediately upon every issuance; zero unrecorded movements. Manage parts returns from technicians (unused or incorrect parts); update IMS accordingly. Inventory Management & Reconciliation Reconcile physical spare parts stock against IMS records on a weekly basis. Identify slow-moving, expired, or obsolete parts and flag to Lead, Inventory Support. Raise a formal replenishment request when stock falls to the defined reorder threshold. Reporting & Documentation Generate weekly spare parts consumption and stock-position reports for the Lead, Inventory Support. Maintain a complete issuance log linking each spare part to its Job Card and technician. Track Part-Failure data to support procurement and OEM quality feedback. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain proper zoning, labelling, and cleanliness of the spare parts storage area at all times. Enforce segregation of duty: no self-authorised issuance. Support all scheduled and spot-check inventory counts. Requirements  Minimum of OND in a related discipline  At least 2-year experience in inventory operations. Good computer skills. Must know the Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word and PowerPoint)  Ability to work with limited supervision.  Strong attention to detail and accuracy. Proficiency in inventory management systems and workflow applications. Experience handling large volumes of items  Excellent organizational and record-keeping skills. Effective communication and stakeholder coordination. Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.

title: Inventory Support Officer - South South
description: Who We are Moniepoint Inc is a financial technology company digitizing Africa’s real economy by building a financial ecosystem for businesses, providing them with all the payment, banking, credit and business management tools they need to succeed.  What We do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community, dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We have several products that provide essential services for businesses such as credit, overdrafts etc. We leverage artificial intelligence and data to make our decisions but also have the technology and data-driven best practices used to support our businesses.  1A. Inventory Support Officer – POS Terminals Role Purpose The ISO (Terminals) is the dedicated custodian for all forms of POS terminals flowing through the repair pipeline. The role ensures end-to-end traceability, enforces custody controls, and maintains absolute logical–physical alignment within the Repair Centre's IMS subsystem, covering every stage from receipt of faulty units to dispatch of QA-cleared OK devices. Key Responsibilities Intake & Receipt Management Receive faulty/returned terminals from state offices; verify against the recall waybill at serial-number level before accepting into the IMS. Log all received devices in the IMS with correct status within 24 hours of physical arrival. Identify and quarantine damaged or missing-serial devices; raise a Discrepancy Report immediately. Repair Pipeline Tracking Push faulty devices to technicians daily and update IMS status to 'In Repair' upon assignment. Monitor movement of each terminal through all repair stages: Assessment → In Repair → Awaiting QA → QA Cleared → Dispatch Holding. Enforce the 24–72-hour SLA from receipt-to-assignment and from QA clearance-to-dispatch readiness. QA Integration & Status Management Receive QA-approved terminals and update IMS status to 'QA Cleared – Awaiting Dispatch' within 4 hours. Flag devices that fail QA back to the repair queue or classify as 'Beyond Economic Repair (BER)' with a written justification report. Ensure all 'BER' devices are tagged and isolated in the scrap/disposal holding area. Dispatch & Outbound Logistics Generate the Dispatch List and Waybill for QA-cleared refurbished and OK devices; obtain approval from Repair Centre Manager and Cluster lead before release. Scan all devices at serial level during physical loading; update IMS to 'In Transit – Outbound'. Confirm receipt acknowledgment from the destination state SIO and close the dispatch transaction in IMS. Inventory Counts & Reconciliation Conduct daily physical counts of all terminals in the repair centre; reconcile against IMS records. Escalate any variance (physical vs. logical) to the Lead, Inventory Support within the same business day. Participate in monthly, quarterly, and annual wall-to-wall counts as directed by the Inventory & Warehouse Manager. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain clearly labelled racks and segregated zones: Faulty, Under-Repair, Refurbished/OK, BER/Scrap. Enforce all provisions of the POS Inventory Control SOP within the repair centre. Uphold audit readiness, workplace safety, and environmental handling standards at all times. Reporting Line Functional: Lead, Inventory Support (Regional) Operational: Repair Centre Manager Dotted: Regional Inventory & Warehouse Manager   1B. Inventory Support Officer – Spare Parts Role Purpose The ISO (Spare Parts) manages the complete lifecycle of all repair consumables — batteries, screens, cables, and accessories — within the repair centre. The role ensures that technicians have the right parts at the right time, waste is minimised, and all issues are fully documented and traceable. Key Responsibilities Spare Parts Receipt & Storage Receive all incoming spare parts consignments; verify at batch/serial level against the accompanying delivery note before logging into IMS. Store spare parts in designated, labelled bins organised by part type and model compatibility. Ensure storage conditions protect electronic components from moisture, dust, and extreme temperature. Issuance Control Issue spare parts ONLY against an approved Job Card raised by a technician and validated by the Repair Centre Manager. Update IMS stock levels immediately upon every issuance; zero unrecorded movements. Manage parts returns from technicians (unused or incorrect parts); update IMS accordingly. Inventory Management & Reconciliation Reconcile physical spare parts stock against IMS records on a weekly basis. Identify slow-moving, expired, or obsolete parts and flag to Lead, Inventory Support. Raise a formal replenishment request when stock falls to the defined reorder threshold. Reporting & Documentation Generate weekly spare parts consumption and stock-position reports for the Lead, Inventory Support. Maintain a complete issuance log linking each spare part to its Job Card and technician. Track Part-Failure data to support procurement and OEM quality feedback. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain proper zoning, labelling, and cleanliness of the spare parts storage area at all times. Enforce segregation of duty: no self-authorised issuance. Support all scheduled and spot-check inventory counts. Requirements  Minimum of OND in a related discipline  At least 2-year experience in inventory operations. Good computer skills. Must know the Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word and PowerPoint)  Ability to work with limited supervision.  Strong attention to detail and accuracy. Proficiency in inventory management systems and workflow applications. Experience handling large volumes of items  Excellent organizational and record-keeping skills. Effective communication and stakeholder coordination. Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.

title: Key Account Officer
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.   As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. You will get to know how each customer operates, build trust with the people who make decisions, and help them get value from Moniepoint’s products. You will monitor account performance, spot risks early and coordinate the right teams to resolve issues. You will also identify opportunities to help customers grow through products that meet their needs. This is a hands-on role that combines customer engagement, field visits, commercial judgment and dependable follow-through.   What you’ll get to do  Build active relationships with assigned businesses and understand their locations, decision makers, priorities, product usage and revenue contribution. Maintain the required contact and visit cadence, recording material conversations, commitments and next steps. Monitor revenue, transaction activity and product usage; investigate unusual changes and raise potential risks early. Identify customer needs, introduce relevant Moniepoint products and qualify opportunities before involving product specialists. Work with Business Relationship Managers (BRMs) and internal teams to coordinate onboarding, training, product adoption and service recovery. Keep customers informed during escalations, follow through with the teams responsible and confirm that issues are resolved. Maintain accurate CRM profiles, stakeholder maps, opportunities, risks and action plans. Share useful competitor and market intelligence with your State or Regional Lead. Support local engagement for strategic accounts under the direction of their primary strategic account owner.   Qualifications  Bachelor’s degree  At least 3 years of experience in B2B account management, banking, fintech, payments, customer success or field sales. A track record of managing a customer portfolio and meeting commercial or service goals. Confidence working with performance data, CRM tools, structured customer meetings and field visits. A relevant tertiary qualification or equivalent practical experience. Strong communication, problem-solving and negotiation skills. The ability to take ownership of customer issues and follow through across multiple teams.   Relevant Skills    Key account and relationship management Customer retention and growth Product adoption and opportunity identification Data analysis and CRM management Issue resolution and escalation Stakeholder management Field engagement and customer communication   What we can offer you  Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human.  Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks.  Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits.  What to expect in the hiring process  A preliminary phone call with the recruiter  An interview with one of our credit business leads  A behavioral and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.  Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Lead, Compliance Quality Assurance
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: Lead, Compliance Quality Assurance Department: Regulatory Compliance  Reports to: Head, Compliance Quality Assurance About this role As the Lead, Compliance Quality Assurance, you are the tactical backbone of our quality assessment framework. You will spearhead the day-to-day operations of our QA Assessor team, transforming quality assurance into a catalyst for operational excellence. Through rigorous standard enforcement and precision-based calibration, you will ensure that Moniepoint’s critical divisions including KYC/Due Diligence, AML, LEA, Transaction Monitoring, and Fraud consistently meet SLAs and regulatory policy standards. Acting as the final line of defense against compliance drift, you are dedicated to maintaining flawless execution, high-velocity accuracy, and total regulatory integrity across all operational touchpoints. Responsibilities Supervise, train, and manage QA Assessors, ensuring consistent grading and execution through regular file calibration exercises.  Lead the secondary review process across the 'Six Pillars' (AML/Transaction Monitoring, Regulatory Control/LEA, and Forensic Fraud), identifying vulnerabilities in accuracy, speed, and regulatory compliance.  Maintain a centralized Compliance Defect Log and translate QA findings into actionable weekly feedback for operational Team Leads to drive continuous improvement.  Perform deep-dive analyses on compliance misses to differentiate between system threshold errors and investigator oversight, recommending necessary process adjustments.  Assist in coordinating internal and external audits by providing evidence of QA testing integrity and ensuring high-quality, audit-ready data. Experience & Background 2–4 years of progressive experience in Compliance QA, Financial Crime Investigation, or EDD/CDD within a FinTech, or commercial bank.  Must have at least 2 years of experience in a supervisory or team lead capacity.  Bachelor’s degree in Law, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field. Skills & Competencies Advanced proficiency in Compliance tools and data analysis using SQL and Excel.  Comprehensive understanding of Nigerian regulatory frameworks (AML/CFT), instant payment fraud, card/POS fraud typologies, and legal protocols for handling Law Enforcement Agency (LEA) and CDD, EDD and Customer screening.  Professional certification such as DCP, CAMS, CFE, or ICA International Diploma is an added advantage. What success looks like in this role Maintenance of flawless execution, high-velocity accuracy, and total regulatory integrity across all operational touchpoints.  Consistent meeting of SLAs and regulatory policy standards across KYC/Due Diligence, AML, LEA, Transaction Monitoring, and Fraud divisions.  Prevention of compliance drift through rigorous standard enforcement and precision-based calibration.  Transformation of quality assurance processes into a true catalyst for operational excellence. Why join us Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities. Fully remote work culture and support for professional development.

title: Metadata & Data Lineage Specialist
description: Who we are  Moniepoint is an all-in-one digital financial services platform powering businesses across emerging markets. Since 2019, our technology has enabled over one million businesses to thrive through comprehensive payment, banking, credit, and business management solutions. Operating through its subsidiaries—including Moniepoint MFB and TeamApt Ltd—Moniepoint processes the majority of Nigeria's POS transactions, representing over $170 billion in annualised Total Payment Volume (TPV). Recognised as Africa’s second-fastest-growing fintech platform and named the Most Inclusive Payment Platform by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) in 2022, Moniepoint continues to scale its profitable financial ecosystem. About this role We are looking for a Metadata & Data Lineage Specialist to build out and run the organization's metadata management and data lineage capabilities. You will be the person who makes our data catalogue genuinely useful — helping teams find, trust, and understand the data they are working with, and tracing exactly how that data moves and transforms across our systems. You will take our metadata management and data lineage frameworks from paper to practice: growing coverage, improving quality, automating collection wherever possible, and building lineage that holds up for our most critical data products, regulatory submissions, and business-critical flows. Responsibilities Metadata Management & Data Cataloguing: Maintain and enhance enterprise metadata, developing business glossaries, data definitions, and ownership frameworks within DataHub. Identify gaps and ensure metadata changes align with governance processes. Data Lineage Management: Develop, maintain, and validate end-to-end data lineage for critical data flows, products, reports, and customer journeys across source systems, ETL/ELT pipelines, and downstream consumers. DataHub Platform & Integration: Support the administration and optimisation of DataHub. Configure ingestion workflows, monitor metadata ingestion jobs, and identify opportunities to improve coverage through automation and APIs. Metadata Quality & Governance: Establish metadata quality rules and KPIs. Perform regular assessments to highlight gaps, support data impact assessments, and ensure alignment with enterprise governance policies. Data Classification & Privacy: Apply data classification metadata based on sensitivity and regulatory requirements. Support Risk, Compliance, and InfoSec teams with necessary lineage information for assessments. AI & Advanced Data Discovery: Drive the adoption of AI-assisted metadata management to automate capture, classification, and enrichment. Contribute to the development of semantic models and knowledge graphs. Stakeholder Engagement: Act as a subject matter expert, facilitating workshops and providing guidance to data producers and consumers to improve overall data literacy and DataHub adoption. Experience & Background Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Management, Data Science, Information Systems, Library/Information Science, Engineering, or a related discipline. 3–6+ years of experience in Metadata Management, Data Governance, Data Architecture, or Data Engineering. Demonstrable hands-on experience with Solidatus, Informatica, DataHub, or a comparable enterprise data catalog platform. Practical experience developing end-to-end data lineage across complex data environments. Deep familiarity with modern data architectures (Medallion, Data Mesh, Data Vault 2.0, warehouses, data lakes, cloud platforms). Experience in financial services, fintech, payments, banking, or another highly regulated data environment is highly desirable. Skills & Competencies Strong proficiency working with technical and business metadata, business glossaries, data domains, and data classification. Experience working with relational databases and a solid understanding of SQL and database structures. Knowledge of APIs, ETL/ELT pipelines, and automated metadata integration. Familiarity with AI-assisted metadata management, semantic modelling, ontologies, and knowledge graph concepts. Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to facilitate training and influence adoption. Professional certification in Data Management or Architecture (e.g., DAMA CDMP, CIMP, DCAM) or related platform certifications are advantageous. What success looks like in this role The enterprise data catalogue is accurate, easily discoverable, and heavily utilised by cross-functional teams to understand data assets. End-to-end data lineage is robust, validated, and actively supports critical data products, regulatory submissions, and incident investigations. Metadata collection is highly automated, maintaining strict quality standards and governance controls with minimal manual intervention. Data literacy and platform adoption (DataHub) scale across the organisation through effective stakeholder enablement. What we can offer you Culture -We put our people first and prioritise the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter A technical interview with the hiring manager A behavioural and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.  Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Product Auditor
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. What We Do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We leverage artificial intelligence and data-driven best practices to support our businesses, from providing credit and overdrafts to ensuring every transaction is secure. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Role Overview The Product Auditor provides independent assurance over the design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of product controls across payment, wallet, settlement, switches and other related products across the organisation The role ensures that new and existing products are deployed with adequate financial, operational, security, and regulatory controls, safeguarding the organization against revenue leakage, settlement failures, regulatory breaches, and technology-driven risks. The Product Auditor will independently evaluate product risk exposure and control maturity prior to scale. Key Responsibilities  Audit Universe & Risk-Based Planning Maintain a living Product Audit Universe covering all payment products, features, and integrations ranked by risk.  Own the annual Product Audit Plan, ensuring coverage is allocated dynamically based on risk ratings, product complexity, regulatory sensitivity, and change velocity. Product Design & Control Assurance Review PRDs, business rules, and transaction workflows to identify logic gaps, unmitigated risk paths, and missing exception-handling routines before products reach production/go-live.  Analyse product path scenarios, verify Maker-Checker enforcement, and provide formal control design sign-off before any material release goes live. Live Product Assessment ( Continuous Audit Review) Periodically assess live payment products to confirm they continue to operate within approved design parameters.  Detect configuration drift, identify silent divergence from original PRDs, and analyse live transaction data for emerging risk patterns. Go-Live Readiness & Control Gate Execute mandatory pre-production Product Audit reviews as an independent control gate for all material releases.  Confirm reconciliation logic, exception queues, and fallback controls are tested and functional.  Escalate critical deficiencies with risk ratings and hold recommendations where a product is not safe to release. Transaction Logic & Mathematical Integrity Interrogate the Fee Engine using SQL to mathematically prove that commissions, VAT, discounts, and splits are posted with complete precision.  Validate duplicate prevention mechanisms and ensure transaction integrity within complex, multi-step payment sequences, and test reversal, refund, and chargeback logic to confirm financial symmetry is maintained in every scenario. Settlement & Ledger Integrity Trace fund flows, confirming continuous synchronisation between wallet sub-ledgers and the General Ledger.  Assess reconciliation logic for breaks and evaluate the authorisation, documentation, and reversibility of manual settlement overrides. Product Change & Configuration Integrity Confirm that all product modifications: fee tables, routing rules, limit parameters passed through an approved change management cycle.  Identify silent changes made outside formal release processes and audit the integrity of product master data to ensure it is access-controlled, version-tracked, and consistent with approved product terms. Vendor & Third-Party Product Risk Assess controls over vendor-managed product components, evaluate SLA performance against contractual commitments, and identify single-vendor dependency risks within critical payment flows.  Evaluate the organisation's ability to detect unilateral changes in third-party API behaviour, fee logic, or settlement processes. Control Advisory & Stakeholder Engagement Engage product and engineering teams early in the design cycle to provide informal control advisory, reducing findings at the formal review stage without compromising independence.  Participate in design reviews and architecture discussions, and build a control-by-design culture across product teams.  Incident Review, RCA & Regulatory Alignment Lead post-incident reviews for product failures,producing structured RCA reports that identify underlying logic failures, not just surface symptoms.  Assess corrective actions for adequacy and track findings to verify closure.  Ensure product logic complies with CBN guidelines, PCI DSS, and consumer protection obligations at the design level, and evaluate the regulatory impact of new features before release. Reporting & Governance Prepare risk-rated audit reports for Executive Management and the Audit Committee, leading with findings, financial impact, and required action.  Maintain a Product Risk Register, deliver quarterly control maturity updates, and ensure governance bodies are never surprised by a product failure that was visible at the design or portfolio review stage. Required Knowledge & Skills  Technical Skills Advanced SQL for independent data extraction and transaction interrogation Payment systems architecture : Wallets, card processing, direct debit, settlement, and reconciliation API and integration literacy (Basic) End-to-end transaction lifecycle knowledge: Authorisation, posting, clearing, settlement, and exception handling PRD and process flow analysis: translating product documentation into control flowcharts Mathematical precision: fee calculations, interest computations, and split payment structures Pattern recognition: detecting anomalies, outliers, and irregularities in large transaction datasets Audit & Risk Skills Risk-based audit methodology: IIA Standards and COSO framework applied to financial products. Control design logic and evaluation Root cause analysis Regulatory knowledge: CBN payment system regulations, PCI DSS, NDPR,Nigerian consumer protection obligations etc Interpersonal & Professional Skills Stakeholder engagement Professional scepticism and independence Risk-rated report writing Tools & Platforms SQL (PostgreSQL / MySQL / MSSQL) AdvancedExcel / Google Sheets Claude / AI Tools Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Finance, or a related quantitative discipline Experience: 3–5+ years in Product Audit, Systems Audit, Financial Data Analytics, or Payment Operations within a fintech or financial services environment Certifications: CISA, CIA, or CFE preferred. ACA / ACCA is acceptable when combined with strong technical product experience and data analytics. Sector Knowledge: Demonstrated hands-on familiarity with payment product architecture, wallet systems, and regulated payment flows in a Nigerian or comparable market context. What We Offer You Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’re human, we listen, and we look out for one another. Learning: We’re big on growth. You’ll find an environment focused on knowledge sharing, training, and helping you reach your potential. Compensation: You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, and an annual bonus, along with other great benefits. What to Expect in the Hiring Process A preliminary phone call with our recruiter. An interview with the hiring team. A final conversation with a member of our executive team. Moniepoint Inc. is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Product Design Manager - Design System
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial ecosystem, helping 10 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, and business management tools since 2019. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, it powers most of the country’s Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Through its subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes $22 billion monthly for its customers while operating profitably. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. About the role  Designing for money means designing for trust. Our customers are shop owners, traders and entrepreneurs, and many are new to digital products. They work on low-end devices and unreliable networks, where one confusing screen can cost them a sale. Your team's work has to hold up for them, whatever their ability or device. You make sure it does.  As a Design Manager, you'll lead a small team of product designers and be accountable for everything they ship: its quality, how it works as one product, and the results it drives for our customers and the business. Your team works either on the products our customers use on POS, mobile and web, or on the operational tools our teams use to serve them.  It is a hands-on role: you build the systems the team works within and step into the hardest problems yourself.  What you'll do  Set the design direction for your area, turn it into plans with milestones and measurable outcomes, and make the case for it to senior leaders in customer and business terms. Work with product partners so every designer begins from a clear, well-framed brief, and push back early when one isn't ready.  Keep each customer journey whole across teams, and resolve conflicting designs before they launch.  Run critique and design reviews against a definition of done that includes accessibility, and stay close enough to the work that nothing reaches customers below the bar. Decide what must be tested with customers before build and what can ship and be measured after, and plan that validation into delivery with success metrics defined up front. Make sure journeys use the design system, with market and product variations handled inside it rather than as one-off rebuilds. Plan and staff system contributions like any other project. Build trusted partnerships with product and engineering, so design shapes what gets built, and design and engineering stay in step through build.  Hire well, set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and build a growth path for each designer.  Bring AI tools into the team's design process, model effective and responsible use in your own work, and build that fluency across the team.  What you'll need to succeed  10+ years of experience in product design, with a portfolio of shipped work across mobile and web that shows the problem, your decisions and the results.  3+ years of experience managing product designers, including hiring, coaching and career development.  Experience setting design direction for a product area and leading a team to deliver it. Experience running a design quality practice, such as critique, design reviews and a definition of done, that raised the quality of shipped work.  Experience building shared patterns or templates adopted across teams, products or markets. Experience shipping accessible, inclusive products for people with disabilities, people new to digital products and people on limited devices and connectivity.  Experience using AI tools in design work and building that fluency across a team.  Nice to have  Experience designing for POS terminals is a strong plus. Experience in financial services, multiple markets or operational tools is also welcome.  What you will get: A leadership role in shaping the future of fintech - your work will impact millions of users. Career growth opportunities. A culture of experimentation - we encourage innovative thinking and rapid iteration. Competitive compensation and benefits. Remote-friendly work culture, with access to learning resources. What to expect in the hiring process  Recruiter conversation. Your background, what you want next, and practical details. 2. Case study review. Walk a design leader through one or two case studies in depth: one from your own work, one from a team you led.  Leadership challenge. Work through a product and team problem live with two design leaders.  Final interview. A conversation with the hiring manager. Why Join Us Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities. Fully remote work culture and support for professional development. What to expect in the hiring process Application & portfolio review: we assess your experience, leadership impact, and Design System case studies that demonstrate strategic thinking, process, and measurable outcomes. Preliminary phone call with recruiter: a brief conversation to discuss your background, leadership experience, and expectations. Interview with senior leadership: a deep dive into your leadership approach, design philosophy, and ability to drive impact. title: Product Design Manager - UX

Our customers are shop owners, traders and entrepreneurs, and many are new to digital products. They work on low-end devices and unreliable networks, where one confusing screen can cost them a sale. Your team's work has to hold up for them, whatever their ability or device. You make sure it does. As a Design Manager, you'll lead a small team of product designers and be accountable for everything they ship: its quality, how it works as one product, and the results it drives for our customers and the business. Your team works either on the products our customers use on POS, mobile and web, or on the operational tools our teams use to serve them. Work with product partners so every designer begins from a clear, well-framed brief, and push back early when one isn't ready. Keep each customer journey whole across teams, and resolve conflicting designs before they launch.  Run critique and design reviews against a definition of done that includes accessibility, and stay close enough to the work that nothing reaches customers below the bar. Decide what must be tested with customers before build and what can ship and be measured after, and plan that validation into delivery with success metrics defined up front. Make sure journeys use the design system, with market and product variations handled inside it rather than as one-off rebuilds. Plan and staff system contributions like any other project. Build trusted partnerships with product and engineering, so design shapes what gets built, and design and engineering stay in step through build.  Hire well, set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and build a growth path for each designer. title: Regional Lead, Client Implementation
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. What We Do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We leverage artificial intelligence and data-driven best practices to support our businesses, from providing credit and overdrafts to ensuring every transaction is secure. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Job Purpose The Implementation Lead is responsible for building, managing, and continuously improving a high-performing regional team of Implementation agents. This role drives the strategic execution of Moniebook's customer onboarding programme at scale, ensuring that every new retail customer in the region is successfully activated, trained, and transitioned into a confident, long-term user of the Moniebook solution. Operating at the intersection of people leadership, operational excellence, and customer success strategy, the Implementation Lead sets performance standards, develops team capability, removes escalation blockers, and partners cross-functionally with Sales, Product, and Account Management to deliver a world-class onboarding experience. Success is measured by team-wide activation rates, time-to-value benchmarks, retention outcomes, and the quality of customer handoffs across the region measure success. Key Responsibilities Team Leadership & Performance Management Recruit, onboard, coach, and retain a regional team of Implementation Agents, fostering a culture of accountability, customer obsession, and continuous improvement. Set clear individual and team performance goals aligned to activation rates, time-to-value, feature adoption, CSAT scores, and churn reduction targets. Conduct regular 1:1s, team reviews, and performance evaluations; identify skill gaps and build development plans to close them. Onboarding Strategy & Programme Oversight Design scalable onboarding frameworks that allow the team to manage growing customer volumes without compromising on quality or personalisation. Define and maintain onboarding milestones, success metrics, and quality standards across all customer segments. Identify opportunities to streamline onboarding timelines and reduce time-to-value without sacrificing adoption depth. Escalation Management & Issue Resolution Act as the first point of escalation for complex technical issues, difficult customer situations, or onboarding stalls that agents are unable to resolve independently. Partner with Product, Engineering, and Support teams to drive resolution of systemic issues affecting onboarding outcomes across the region. Maintain clear escalation pathways and SLA standards, ensuring customers always feel supported and informed during issue resolution. Cross-functional Collaboration Partner closely with the Sales team to ensure smooth pre-to-post sale handoffs and that customer expectations are properly set before onboarding begins. Collaborate with Account Managers to refine the handoff process, ensuring agents provide complete, high-quality context that enables seamless long-term retention. Work with the Product team to surface recurring customer pain points, usability gaps, and feature adoption blockers, acting as a regional voice of the customer. Data, Reporting & Insights Track and analyse team-wide performance data including activation rates, onboarding completion timelines, feature adoption depth, CSAT scores, and early-stage churn metrics. Produce regular reports for senior leadership on regional onboarding health, trends, risks, and improvement initiatives. Use data to identify underperforming segments, agents, or onboarding touchpoints, and drive targeted interventions to address root causes. Process Improvement & Innovation Continuously review and refine onboarding processes, tools, and resources to improve efficiency, consistency, and customer outcomes. Champion the adoption of new technologies, automation, or methodologies that can enhance the team's ability to deliver high-touch onboarding at scale. Build a feedback loop between frontline agent insights and senior leadership/product decisions to ensure ground-level learnings influence the business. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Operations, or a related field (or equivalent experience). 4 - 6 years of experience in customer onboarding, customer success, or implementation roles, with at least 2–3 years in a team lead or people management capacity. Proven track record of leading onboarding or CS teams to consistently achieve activation, adoption, and retention targets, ideally within SaaS, retail technology, or fintech. Strong people leadership skills with the ability to motivate, develop, and hold a distributed team accountable for outcomes. Excellent analytical skills, able to interpret customer health data, team performance metrics, and identify actionable trends. Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills; able to present to senior leadership, navigate cross-functional relationships, and represent the customer voice persuasively. Deep customer empathy combined with a results-driven orientation. Highly organised with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, and escalations simultaneously without compromising quality. Comfortable working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments; brings structure and clarity without over-engineering. Preferred Qualifications Experience building or scaling onboarding teams from the ground up in a high-growth technology company. Exposure to retail operations, merchant services, or point-of-sale technology. Experience designing training curricula, onboarding playbooks, or knowledge management systems. Familiarity with customer health scoring methodologies, NPS/CSAT frameworks, or CS operations best practices. About You You are a natural leader who takes genuine pride in developing the people around you, and you measure your success by the success of your team and your customers. You are strategic and execution-focused; you can zoom out to design the right system and zoom in to resolve a customer escalation on the same day. You bring calm, clarity, and decisiveness under pressure. When things go wrong, your team looks to you and finds confidence, not panic. You are deeply data-literate; you use numbers to tell stories, make decisions, and hold yourself and your team accountable. You are a collaborative partner who builds trust across functions, Sales, Product, Support, and Account Management, and all see you as an ally, not a blocker. You thrive in environments where the playbook is still being written, and you take ownership of writing it. You are customer-obsessed at scale, even as you move further from direct customer interaction, you never lose sight of the human beings behind the metrics. What Success Looks Like Your regional team consistently achieves 90%+ customer activation rates within the 30–60 day onboarding window, month over month. Average time-to-live for customers in your region is at or below the 1–2 week target, with no systemic delays attributed to onboarding execution gaps. Regional post-onboarding CSAT scores average 4.5+, and your team's handoff quality is rated as excellent by Account Managers. Early-stage churn (within 90 days post-onboarding) for customers in your region remains below 5%. Your agents are among the most skilled and engaged at Moniebook, attrition on your team is low, development is visible, and performance is strong. You have documented, improved, and operationalised at least two significant enhancements to the regional onboarding playbook each quarter. What we can offer you Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning: We have a learning-and-development-focused environment, with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation: You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter. An interview with the operations lead. A behavioural and technical interview with the business lead. Moniepoint is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Job Purpose The Regional Security Lead ensures that our mission never stops. You are the guardian of our physical spaces, ensuring that every Moniepoint office is a sanctuary where our team can build and create without worry. By leading regional security operations, managing on-ground teams, and proactively identifying risks, you provide the stability and safety that allows financial happiness to thrive. You don't just react to incidents; you build the systems that prevent them. Key Responsibilities Safeguard our People and Assets: Lead the implementation of security policies that protect our team, offices, and equipment across your region. Master the Environment: Conduct regular security assessments to spot vulnerabilities and design innovative strategies to reduce risk. Lead the Front Line: Supervise and mentor private security guards and armed police personnel, ensuring they perform their duties with mastery and respect. Build Strong Alliances: Act as our primary liaison with law enforcement and emergency services, ensuring we always have a seat at the table during emergencies. Investigate and Solve: Lead the response to security breaches and accidents, providing clear, factual reports that help us learn and improve. Empower the Team: Design and deliver training programs that equip our security personnel and employees with life-saving protocols. Innovate for Safety: Stay ahead of security trends and technology (like CCTV and access control) to keep our regional operations modern and resilient. Support Business Resilience: Provide expert guidance on asset recovery and fraud investigation when the business needs your mastery. Qualifications Professional Background: Should have at least 5 years of experience successfully leading a security team in a guard services/physical security company or have 5 years of experience as an ex-commissioned service personnel supervisor—either in the military, police, or paramilitary. Education: A Bachelor’s degree in Criminology, Psychology, Criminal Justice, or a related field. Certification: You hold a recognized security certification such as CPP, PSP, or CPO. Integrity: A clean criminal record and the ability to pass a comprehensive background check are essential. Language & Culture: You speak the local dialects of the major tribes in your assigned region, allowing you to connect with the community. Good experience working with automated security systems like CCTV cameras, burglary alarm systems, etc. About You You are a Hero: You are driven by mastery and the desire to protect others. People count on you to come through when things get tough. You are Relatable: You don’t hide behind technical jargon. You communicate clearly and build trust with everyone, from the security guards to the executive team. You are Proactive: You don’t wait for things to go wrong. You have the "Creator" spirit, always looking for better ways to secure our future.  You are composed: In high-pressure situations, you are the calmest person in the room. You lead with facts, not emotions. What Success Looks Like Zero Preventable Incidents: Our regional offices remain safe, secure, and fully operational. High Readiness: Security personnel are well-trained and respond to drills or real-world events with 100% precision. Strong Community Ties: You have built a network of local stakeholders that helps Moniepoint navigate regional risks effectively. Operational Excellence: Security technology is 100% functional, and documentation is factual, honest, and actionable. What we can offer you Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all voices are heard, and we look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning: We have a learning- and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing and training. Compensation: You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, and an annual bonus, plus other benefits. Moniepoint Inc. is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Senior Content Designer
description: About Us: Moniepoint Group is a financial technology company digitizing Africa’s real economy by building a financial ecosystem for businesses, providing them with all the payment, banking, credit and business management tools they need to succeed. At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community, dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We have several products that provide essential services for businesses such as credit, overdrafts, bank integration, payment gateway, etc. We leverage artificial intelligence and data to make our decisions, but also have the technology and data-driven best practices used to support our businesses. About this role: As a Senior Content Designer, you take ownership of the quality and strategic direction of content across your squad or product area. You bring expert content design judgment, deep user insight, and a collaborative mindset to shape product experiences that are clear, inclusive, and emotionally engaging. You support junior content designers, influence cross-team content strategy, and play a vital role in driving alignment across product, design, and engineering. You display an exceptional grasp of design thinking and content design expertise and are comfortable delivering well-thought out ideas to senior stakeholders and driving content design strategy each day.  What you’ll do  You are responsible for end-to-end content design strategy and execution on a project, from discovery through delivery, launch, and ongoing iteration. Partnering closely with product managers, product designers, and engineers to embed content strategy in product discovery and delivery, shaping scope, trade-offs, and sequencing. Define for exceptional, accessible, and inclusive content that builds trust, clarity, and meaningful user engagement. Comfortable wireframing and prototyping and delivering your work in Figma, with clear rationale, adhering to a design systems and content design principles. Craft high-quality content for complex product flows, interface text, microcopy, error messaging, help content, and documentation, setting the bar for tone, clarity, and consistency. Take a strong role in qualitative and quantitative research methods (user interviews, usability tests, A/B experiments, content audits, analytics) using insight as a core design input. Strong stakeholder management skills are a must for this role.  You must be able to work in a fast-changing environment where processes are still being defined.  Exceptional knowledge of content design principles and end-to-end product thinking.  Experience with A/B testing, UX metrics, and data interpretation and the ability to drive your own research initiatives.  Exceptional product intuition - understanding user needs, business constraints, and technical feasibility. Great if you’ve built workflows/tools using AI.  Excellent knowledge of working in cross-functional teams. Strong communication skills - able to explain the “why” behind your decisions  Strong stakeholder management is a must for this role  Recruitment Process Application & portfolio review - we’re looking for exceptional content design case studies, showing examples of end-to-end product thinking, driven by research and illustrating impact.  Recruiter conversation - light intro on your background, team experience, and motivations. title: Senior Principal, Talent Marketing
description: About us Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times as Africa's fastest-growing fintech, Moniepoint is trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of dollars in transactions monthly. Where Moniepoint is not yet an established consumer brand, you will solve complex talent acquisition problems by understanding how senior engineers, engineering managers, and technical leaders think, connect, and evaluate career moves across Europe. Working from a blank piece of paper with high autonomy, you will translate our global Employer Value Proposition (EVP) into localized, high-converting talent marketing strategies. Developer Platform Immersion: Leverage deep knowledge of where engineers consume information (e.g., GitLab/GitHub communities, tech forums, Discord/Slack groups, Meetup, Eventbrite) to drive authentic engagement. 3. Technical EVP Translation: Translate technical architecture, distributed systems challenges, and fintech infrastructure realities into authentic, intellectually rigorous technical messaging that outshines local competitors. Performance, Analytics & Optimization Hiring-Centric Metrics: Discard vanity metrics. Evaluate every initiative against pipeline contribution, qualified applicant rates, candidate quality score, cost-per-hire, and time-to-fill. Budget Oversight: Own and allocate dedicated talent marketing budgets with extreme commercial discipline—scaling programs that drive measurable hires and rapidly decommissioning initiatives that underdeliver. Paid Acquisition (Tactical Lever): Oversee and strategically deploy paid recruitment marketing spend across relevant technical platforms and channels when targeted outbound and community channels require acceleration. 5. Strategic Leadership & Scalability Strategic Thought Partnership: Serve as the trusted advisor to the Head of Talent Acquisition, VP of Engineering, and Brand Leadership on talent market intelligence, competitor positioning, and developer sentiment. Playbook Documentation: Establish and document Moniepoint's global talent expansion playbook, creating scalable frameworks that will be deployed across future international markets. Zero-to-One Market Entry Track Record: Proven success entering new geographies or scaling talent brand where the employer brand was nascent or non-existent, creating playbooks from a blank sheet of paper. Fintech & Scale Exposure: Experience in hyper-growth fintech, high-frequency/payments infrastructure, or high-scale distributed systems environments. International Collaboration: Experience collaborating with international founding teams or distributed tech hubs across emerging and mature markets. Skills & Competencies Mastery in Event-Driven Pipeline Activation: Extensive hands-on experience designing and executing physical and digital developer events and architecting the subsequent candidate nurturing journey that yields hires. Deep Engineering Domain Fluency: Genuine understanding of software engineering culture, tech stacks (distributed systems, backend, infra, DevOps), and developer channels (Meetup, Eventbrite, GitLab/GitHub, Reddit, tech conferences). Comfort with Substantial Ambiguity: High agency and entrepreneurial drive; ability to make decisive bets, test hypotheses, and build structure in fast-moving, high-growth environments. Strategic Campaign Design: Ability to connect high-level EVP strategy to pragmatic, sprint-based talent acquisition sprints that deliver on an aggressive hiring plan (500+ tech hires). Paid Digital Campaign Optimization: Direct experience running and optimizing paid digital recruitment advertising campaigns independently across social and developer networks. What success looks like in this role First 30 Days (Discovery & Immersion): Map the competitive landscape and developer talent dynamics in Poland and Spain. Establish alignment with technical hiring leads (PEP, Engineering Directors) and TA leads to define immediate priority pipelines. Audit existing employer brand collateral and identify localized messaging gaps for European tech hiring.
